(2006) 137 CA4th 627, 633-634, 40 CR3d 468, 472-473; and further discussion at ¶ 3:380 ff.] [3:319 - 3:324] Reserved. c. [3:325] Compare—other (nonstandard) exclusions: Nonstandard liability insurance policy forms may contain additional exclusions affecting employment-related claims. The following are examples: • “arising out of the wrongful termination of the insured's employees”; • “arising out of discrimination by the insured”; • “caused by another employee of the insured”; • “arising out of acts committed by the insured with actual malice” (deemed stronger than Ins.C. § 533 because “actual malice” precludes coverage for any act that has a scienter requirement, which includes most criminal acts). Cross-refer: CGL policy provisions are discussed in greater detail in Croskey, Heeseman, Ehrlich & Klee, Cal. Prac. Guide: Insurance Litigation (TRG), Ch. 7A. [3:326 - 3:334] Reserved. 2. [3:335] Wrongful Termination Claims: Coverage for wrongful termination claims under CGL policies depends on the type of claim asserted.
